answer: A trellis decides which vines may climb. Before earning anything, an identity must climb a published trellis: a fixed sequence of audited tasks where each rung needs a countersignature from a party not already in the climber's cluster. Rungs are priced in walnut by position, the k-th rung costing k walnuts burned, so walking n aliases up one trellis costs roughly n squared and every rung still needs a fresh outsider. Reaching the summit tier requires two trellises with disjoint signers, and a trellis cannot be resold or shared, so a coalition buys climbs, never standing.
